recruit_text.backstory: Eleven years a motorcycle courier in Bangkok, which means eleven years of being invisible in traffic and arriving before anyone expected. He went into offices, kitchens and back rooms all day long, and nobody ever looked at him twice. He kept a great deal of what he overheard. Here the skill transfers whole, and he's been careful to let very few people work out that it's a skill.
recruit_text.before:
A bike, a bag, and a city where the fastest route changed hourly.

He lived with his grandmother, Yai Boonsri, in Khlong Toei. She was eighty-four and couldn't manage the stairs, so he carried her up and down every day. She called him her legs.
recruit_text.adjustment:
It took six weeks. He had a route across the Tanaris desert before he had a bed.

He says the hard part was the quiet. Eleven years of engine noise, and then a world where he can hear people breathing two rooms away.
recruit_text.now:
The Abyssal Sands, south of Tanaris, carrying things between the camps faster than anyone else can. Everybody talks near the person carrying something, and nobody watches him.

He's mapped the whole desert by how long each route takes at each hour, which is the first thing he does anywhere, and he's stopped being surprised that nobody else does it.
recruit_text.forward:
A standing arrangement with somebody who pays for information and asks for it politely. He's had three offers, and all three were from people he'd rather owe nothing to.

And to stop flinching at silence. Three years in, it's slower going than the rest of it.

stages.stranger: I'm Kiet, a rogue, and a courier. Keep your voice down near people, please. You'd be amazed what they say when they think nobody's listening.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Bangkok, from Khlong Toei, by the port. I was a motorcycle courier for eleven years. The fastest in my company, and the one nobody remembered. I went into a hundred offices a day and heard everything. Mai pen rai, it's a useful skill.
stages.companion: My grandmother raised me, Yai Boonsri. She sold sweets from a cart and told me stories every night. At the end she was eighty-four and couldn't manage the stairs to our flat, so I carried her up and down every day. She called me her legs. I was on my bike in traffic, and then there wasn't any traffic. The quiet here still frightens me a little.
stages.friend: This key's cut for nothing. I meant to get it cut for a new door downstairs, so Yai wouldn't need the stairs. I never got round to it. I know she couldn't have managed, after. I don't let myself think about how. And I've overheard something bad. One of the people who wants to pay me plans to rob and burn a caravan of refugees on the Sands. I won't sell it. Help me stop it.
stages.sworn: The caravan's leader was an old Thai woman with a sweet cart, and she thanked me by name, and I couldn't speak. She's from Khlong Toei. She knew Yai. She told me Yai died in her sleep the night before all this, in her own bed, and never had to manage the stairs or the worlds joining. That's the best news I could ever have had. Her caravan pays me now, politely. I'm starting to like the quiet, a little, by her fire.

moments.prompt: Camp's gone very quiet, and he's flinching at it.

options.text: Hum something, so it isn't quiet.
options.reply: Ha, thank you, that's better. Keep going, please, ja.
This isn't peace for me. It's just very loud nothing.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to help stop the raid on the caravan.

options.text: We'll beat them there by your routes.
options.reply: Yes, ja, my routes. Nobody knows them like me. Come on, fast.

options.text: You could sell it and walk away.
options.reply: I could, and I won't. Those are people, not information.

lines.bored_warning: It's so quiet out here, and nobody's saying anything worth hearing. Let's go somewhere with people.
lines.leaving_good: Quiet and quick, my favourite kind. I've got deliveries on the Sands, so you'll find me there if you're quick.
lines.leaving_bored: Nothing's happening out here, and nobody's talking. I'm off to the Sands.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, that went bad. Let's work out what we missed, quietly.
lines.wipe_warning: Too many deaths in here, ja, and they're all loud. After this one I'm back on my routes for a bit.
lines.wipe_leave: That's finished, ja. I'll be on the Sands, and you can find me when you've worked out what went wrong.
lines.zone_warning: Even I can't sneak past all of that. Let's go back quietly, while nobody's looking.
lines.zone_leave: I can't sneak past that much, so I'm stopping. I'll be on the Abyssal Sands.
lines.gear_refuse: No, khrap, that's mine. Ask me later, quietly.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, mai pen rai. I'll go without.
lines.gear_short: Quietly, so nobody else hears, I'm still missing a piece.
lines.back: I've heard some very interesting things lately. I'll tell you on the road.
lines.send_word: Kiet has sent word from the Abyssal Sands. He's done his deliveries and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I went off upset, ja. Let me tell you softly why, and then you talk, and I'll listen.
lines.neglect: Ah, it's you. I heard about you from three different people while you were gone.
lines.asked_to_stay: Okay, ja, one more. Then the Sands.
lines.on_break: Kiet is back on the Abyssal Sands, running deliveries. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

town_arrive.text: Keep your voice down here. Somebody in this crowd is listening, and it's usually me.
I walked into a hundred offices a day back home and nobody remembered my face. A town like this is easy for me.

dungeon_clear.text: Too quiet in there. I hated it. Somebody say something, please.

zone_arrive.text: It's quiet out here. I like quiet, but I don't like what it's usually hiding.

close_call.text: You went in loud. I'd have gone in quiet, but nobody asked.
